mike: Heads-up — trying to run our JS SDK inside a Cloudflare Worker and the bundle fails with "could not resolve 'fs'" and some TS errors referencing Node types. Any recommended pattern so customers don't have to add weird esbuild flags?

sophia: Workers are browser-like so best practice is an explicit edge entrypoint. Either an `./edge` export or a tiny `redwood-inference-edge` package that only uses fetch and DOM types.

mike: Right now I hacked `--external:fs --external:net` into wrangler build and used `--platform=browser`. Works but feels hacky.

kai: Two quick things to do in SDK:
1) Add an exports conditional for `./edge` pointing to an ESM file with zero node deps (dist/edge.mjs).
2) Emit a separate typings file (dist/edge.d.ts) that uses DOM `ReadableStream` instead of `NodeJS.ReadableStream`.
That lets bundlers resolve the right entry without users adding flags.

sophia: Also remove or guard Node-specific timer usage in retry logic. Replace `process.nextTick`/`setImmediate` with `globalThis.setTimeout`/helpers so Workers don't crash.

mike: TypeScript pain — even if we ship edge.d.ts, consumers sometimes still pick up main index.d.ts. How to ensure they get the edge types?

kai: Use package.json `exports` mapping with types per subpath or `typesVersions` hack. Example snippet:
```
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" },
  "./edge": { "import": "./dist/edge.mjs", "types": "./dist/edge.d.ts" }
}
```
Then docs instruct `import { createEdgeClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'`.

sophia: Also add a `browser` field in package.json to help older bundlers and a top-level `module` ESM entry to favour modern toolchains.

mike: Crypto helper — many users expect `crypto.randomBytes`. Workers expose `crypto.getRandomValues`. Can we include a tiny helper that returns Uint8Array and document it?

kai: Yes. For edge builds export `randomBytes(n): Uint8Array` implemented with `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(n))`. Avoid Buffer in edge types.

pkg-bot: FYI: there's an internal branch `edge-shim-prototype` with an edge.mjs that strips debug/logging and uses fetch-only transport. CI shows bundle OK locally.

sophia: Docing: add a small `workers-starter` repo and a short Troubleshooting section in SDK README:
- Prefer `import { createEdgeClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` for Workers and other edge runtimes
- If you see Node modules during bundling, check `package.json` exports and set `--platform=browser`
- For wrangler/esbuild: example build: `esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --outfile=dist/worker.js --platform=browser --format=esm`
- If you need env replacements: use `--define:process.env.FOO='\"bar\"'` or pass secrets from the environment at runtime
- Ensure tsconfig `lib` includes `dom` so DOM types are available

mike: Any concerns about header sizes? We sometimes add dev headers for tracing that can push workers past header limits.

kai: Gate dev headers and verbose traces behind an env flag (and avoid very long JSON in headers). Also make SDK not automatically send big metadata headers in edge entry.

ci-bot: Note: PR #4890 opened with edge export + edge typings. Unit tests: 62/64; two node-only tests are skipped in edge matrix. Integration harness with wrangler example added.

sophia: Let's also add a telemetry event when `createEdgeClient` is used (opt-in) so we can track adoption before we deprecate heavy transitive deps in main entry.

mike: I'll draft the workers starter README and the small code snippet for onboarding. Thanks! :rocket:
